questions.stem: A client has an eGFR of 52 mL/min/1.73 m² and a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 180 mg/g on repeat testing more than 4 months apart, with no evidence of acute kidney injury. Which interpretation is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The findings meet criteria for chronic kidney disease because reduced eGFR and albuminuria have persisted for more than 3 months; this is G3a with A2 albuminuria.","B":"The findings indicate acute kidney injury because an eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² is considered acute until a normal creatinine value is documented after treatment.","C":"The findings do not meet CKD criteria because an eGFR above 45 mL/min/1.73 m² is sufficient to exclude chronic kidney disease when albuminuria is under 300 mg/g.","D":"The findings indicate kidney failure because persistent albuminuria with any eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m² places the client in the kidney-failure category."}}
questions.rationale: KDIGO defines chronic kidney disease by abnormalities of kidney structure or function present for at least 3 months. An eGFR of 52 mL/min/1.73 m² falls in G3a, and an albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 180 mg/g falls in A2. Persistence over more than 3 months supports CKD rather than an acute kidney injury.
questions.source_name: KDIGO — 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation and Management of Chronic Kidney Disease
questions.source_detail: KDIGO 2024 remains the current global CKD guideline; CKD requires persistence for at least 3 months and is classified by GFR and albuminuria categories.

qc.qc_note: Strict Wave-5 anti-cue rule: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; correct option is neither unique shortest nor unique longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility and wording cues.
